Layout engine

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Layout engine
PurposeWeb browser rendering
ExamplesBlink, Gecko, WebKit
RelatedHTML, CSS, DOM

A layout engine is the software component of a web browser that turns a document tree plus a set of style rules into boxes with positions on a screen. It sits between the parser and the compositor.[1]

The two inputs are the DOM and the CSS cascade. The engine walks the tree, computes styles, lays out each box with the constraints of its parent, and paints the result.[2]

History

Early engines laid out tables only. Incremental layout arrived when engines learned to mark only the affected subtree as dirty instead of reflowing the whole document.

Incremental layout

An incremental engine keeps a dirty bit per element. When a node changes size, its ancestors are re-laid out, but siblings that cannot move are reused as-is.
